request.spec:
Selected claims can be moved to another person together: a select of the person and a button
beside the bulk buttons. Each selected claim is moved in list order by exactly the rules of moving
one claim (who may, which statuses, closed periods, retirement, with the same CLAIM_REASSIGNED and
rollup lines); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were moved and how many were
refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Selected claims can be moved to another person together: a select of the person and a button
beside the bulk buttons. Each selected claim is moved in list order by exactly the rules of moving
one claim (who may, which statuses, closed periods, retirement, with the same CLAIM_REASSIGNED and
rollup lines); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were moved and how many were
refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
You can now move selected claims to another person in one go, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What's on screen:** a "Move to…" person select (`bulk-reassign-to`) and a "Move selected" button (`bulk-reassign`) sit right after the bulk-settle button. Once the action finishes, the screen shows how many were moved (`bulk-reassigned`) and how many were refused (`bulk-reassign-refused`). The counts are cleared while a new press runs, and the selection is emptied afterwards. It's in `features/bulkreassign/bulkreassign.slot.tsx`.

**What happens on the server:** a new `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/bulk-reassign` endpoint (`ReassignClaims`) goes through the selected claims in list order: people in the order they were added, each person's claims newest first. Each claim gets the same checks as moving a single claim, and is saved and written to the audit file the same way, with its own `CLAIM_REASSIGNED` line and rollup lines. Any claim that fails a check is left as it is and counted as refused. To share the checks, I moved them out of `ApplyReassign` into a helper that both the single and bulk moves use.

**One difference from the single move:** the test expects a claim that already belongs to the chosen person (Ben→Ben) to count as moved and to get a `CLAIM_REASSIGNED … from=Ben to=Ben` line. Moving a single claim refuses that case, so the bulk move allows it as an exception. The claim stays with its person and is just listed as their newest. Moving one claim on its own still refuses a move to its own person.
